To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TNFRI sensitizes neurons to the neuroprotective effects of EPO and VEGF.
TNFRI mediates neuroprotection by EPO and VEGF in cortical neurons and in the brain after stroke and seizure.

TNF receptor I (TNFRI) is necessary for constitutively and glucose deprivation (GD)-induced expression of erythropoietic receptor (EPOR) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and for EPO- and, to a lesser extent, VEGF-mediated protection of cortical neurons from ischemic and excitotoxicty injury.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of molecular pathways and targets that can be used for the development of neuroprotective therapies.
the identification of molecular mechanisms of TNFR-mediated neuroprotection and the development of new strategies for neuroprotection in stroke and neurodegenerative diseases.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the role of TNF in the brain and its potential therapeutic use in neurodegenerative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TNFR1 sensitizes neurons to EPO- and/or VEGF-mediated protection after ischemic and/or excitotoxic insults.
TNFRI sensitizes neurons to neuroprotective actions of EPO and VEGF, which is a new and important mechanism of neuroprotection by TNFRI.
TNFRI sensitizes neurons to neuroprotection by EPO and VEGF, and that this may be relevant in the context of stroke, epilepsy, and other neurological disorders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TNFRI mediates neuroprotection through a variety of pathways, one of which is EPO-VEGF signaling, and that TNFRI KO animals are less protected from excitotoxicity and ischemic injury.
TNFRI mediates neuroprotection by regulating the expression of several neuroprotective genes, and that this effect is mediated by EPO and VEGF, both of which are known to be induced by TNF.
TNFRI mediates EPO- and TNF-induced protection of neurons from ischemic and excitatory insults by up-regulating expression of EPOR, VEGF and other neuroprotective molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TNFRI can be used to enhance EPO- and other neuroprotective factors’ efficacy in neurodegenerative disorders and ischemic stroke.
TNFRI may be a novel target for the design of neuroprotective strategies.
TNFRI plays an essential role in neuroprotection by regulating expression of neurotrophic cytokines and growth factors.
